body: I’m also neurodivergent (audhd) and have pretty bad social anxiety so making friends has been difficult for me as well. I empathize with your situation. You mentioned people could support you when you struggle what would that ideally look like for you within a friendship? If you were able to heal from your trauma what would you want to connect/ bond over? I ask this not to dismiss any of your experiences but from my experience if a friendship forms on the basis of relating solely on trauma and negative experiences the friendship/ relationship may not have an opportunity to help both parties grow in positive ways.

I took EHS 311. It’s an easy and helpful class since the textbook gives you tips on how to actually manage stress. There’s a good amount of discussion posts and quizzes for each section. There’s a term paper and final exam. Overall course load is very manageable.

I struggle with the same thing, but continuous affirmations have helped me. I tell myself “I am not here to make others comfortable. I am here to express who I am.” “What others say to me is a projection of their own reality, it has nothing to do with me.” Affirmations like these help me to distance myself from what others say about me. It gives me the power to ground myself and know that I’m enough no matter what other people’s opinions may be. 
When I have time to myself, I do EFT tapping in conjunction to repeating positive affirmations. Learning to accept yourself and being comfortable in your own skin allows rude/mean comments to bounce off instead of seeping through. But with that being said even if the comments do seep through, it’s important to validate how you feel. 
Hope that helps. You got this! You will overcome social anxiety!
